contamination.brief_line: 有记录的骨架：作者指出，叫魂案让皇帝有理由对抓不到妖首的地方官发怒，而这样的妖首并不存在(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E1)。弘历在朱批中痛斥河南巡抚“无用废物”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E2)，斥浙江巡抚按例把案子交给臬司(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E3)，痛骂未及时报案的江苏按察使吴坛“不知恩之物”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E4)。作者认为官僚中存在多种抵制，包括可能有官员拒绝迫害无辜(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E5)，且抵制不必串通(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E6)。危机前一年，有人说吴绍诗被称为“老菩萨”，弘历担心他消极误事(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E7)；吴时年七十，出身法律世家，弘历很尊重这个家族(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E8)；高晋说没听说吴不称职，弘历让他留任(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E9)。谣言6月中旬从浙江传入江西，吴未奏报，自称口头命令属下警觉，无人被捕(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E10)；弘历只温和地说“汝误矣”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E11)。10月初吴报告布下比别省更严密的警网，派人改装密查(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E12)，并在奏报中警告“左道邪术”之害，弘历朱批“恐属空言，实难信矣”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E13)。六个星期后，吴报告江西没有一起剪辫案，档案中没有江西搜捕嫌犯的记录(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E14)。吴安然度过危机，第二年被任命为刑部尚书(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E16)。对照：其子吴坛同样未报案而遭痛斥(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E17)，三周后查出苏州城外十一座经堂(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E18)；收场时，未及时奏报的苏尔德被贬往新疆(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E19)。

必须写明的不确定性：本文唯一依据是孔飞力《叫魂》中译本（陈兼、刘昶译），这是一部学术史著作，没有使用其他史源。朱批和奏报文字据本书引用（中译本文字，E13中“矣口”照书中原样），是否与档案原文逐字一致无法从本书判断。“吴绍诗根本不打算查缉、部署只是装模作样”是作者的推断(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E15)，作者自己也提出另一种可能，即警网根本抓不到人(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E15)，文章只能写“作者认为……”。吴升官的原因，作者也只是推测可能与他的法律造诣和高晋的袒护有关(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E16)。高晋答应的后续报告作者未能找到(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E9)。不要替吴绍诗或弘历写心理活动。年份照书中写法使用，不要另做换算。

issues.problem: 英文“an emperor who meant every word of his orders”比中文“一位认真追究的皇帝”说得更重。证据只说弘历当时没有察觉案件的荒谬，没有说他对每道命令都字字当真。

evidence.quote: 叫魂案件虽如此荒谬，但弘历在当时却对此并无察觉

issues.proposed: 英文改为“The governors faced an emperor who was in earnest about the hunt, and a quarry that could not be caught.”，与中文对齐。
issues.rationale: 英文末句原写弘历对每道命令都字字当真，证据只说他当时没有察觉案件荒谬。现改为“an emperor who was in earnest about the hunt”，与中文“一位认真追究的皇帝”对齐。中文不变。

issues.problem: 开头直接写“叫魂的谣言”，不了解背景的读者不知道谣言具体指什么。正文到 story.2 才出现“剪辫”。

evidence.quote: 也没有在本省发现剪辫情事

issues.proposed: 可在首次提到时用半句点明，这类谣言与“剪辫”有关（英文 queue-clipping）。不要另加背景。

issues.problem: 稿件把苏尔德受罚写成单纯“收场时被挑出来重罚”，漏掉了孔飞力交代的处罚性质：案子基础崩溃后，弘历在官僚中找替罪羊来结束清剿，并借处罚证明清剿正确。同时受罚的还有富尼汉。缺了这一层，读者会把苏尔德的下场当成对“不报、阻挠”的常规惩处，判断会改变。

evidence.quote: 恼羞成怒的弘历以在官僚中寻找替罪羊来结束对叫魂案的清剿
只有通过处罚这些官员的失职，他才能向世人和后代昭告，他的清剿是正确的
苏尔德被单独挑出来受到特别惩处

issues.proposed: 在首句前补一句：“孔飞力写道，弘历以在官僚中寻找替罪羊来结束清剿，借处罚失职官员证明清剿正确。”然后接现有苏尔德一句。英文同步补入。富尼汉可不展开。
issues.rationale: 在苏尔德一句前补入孔飞力对收场处罚性质的交代：弘历以找替罪羊结束清剿，借处罚失职官员表明清剿正确。中英同步修改，ev 增加 E22。富尼汉没有展开。

issues.problem: “苏尔德的下场则说明，不报和阻挠可以被单独挑出来重罚”省去了孔飞力对这次处罚的定性（收场时找替罪羊、借此证明清剿正确），把它写成了对不报、阻挠的一般后果。

issues.problem: context.1 用“臬司”，story.3 用“按察使”，指的是同一官职，中文读者未必知道二者相同。英文两处都写 judicial commissioner，没有这个问题。

issues.problem: limits.0 与 uncertainty_note 几乎重复同一组限定（唯一史源、装模作样是推断、高晋袒护是推测）。“高晋的后续报告未找到”一项对理解主线帮助不大。
issues.proposed: 保留一处完整说明，另一处压缩为一两句。可删去“高晋答应的后续报告，孔飞力没有找到”。

edits.before: That year the Qianlong emperor, Hongli, pressed provincial officials over their failure to catch the sorcerers' leaders. Philip A. Kuhn, the historian who reconstructed the panic, points out that the emperor could turn his anger on provincial officials who failed to catch those leaders. They could not avoid failing, because no such leader existed. Kuhn also insists that Hongli did not see the absurdity of the case at the time. The governors faced an emperor who meant every word of his orders, and a quarry that could not be caught.

edits.before: The risks are on record too. Hongli wrote "I fear these are empty words" in response to Wu Shaoshi's warning. The Old Bodhisattva nickname, and the worry that he was too passive, had reached the emperor a year before the crisis. Su'erde's fate shows that failing to report and obstructing the campaign could earn an official a heavy punishment of his own. My inference is that Wu Shaoshi got through largely on advantages no one else could borrow. Another official doing the same thing might have received a very different rescript.

Su'erde's fate shows that when the campaign ended and Hongli looked for scapegoats among his officials, those who had failed to report or had obstructed the campaign could be singled out for heavy punishment. My inference is that Wu Shaoshi got through largely on advantages no one else could borrow. Another official doing the same thing might have received a very different rescript.

edits.before: 这也不是一个智者对抗暴君的故事。孔飞力列举过官僚抵制的几种情形：有深思熟虑的，有程序颟顸误了时机的，有因不信其事而轻视此案的，有怕清剿危及仕途的，也可能有耿直官员拒绝依据诬告迫害无辜。他说这些行动不像是协调一致的，抵制专制权力并不需要串通。本文无法据此判定吴绍诗属于哪一种。孔飞力也提醒，说弘历“利用”了政治罪，并不比说政治罪“利用”了他更接近真实。本文作者的一种解读是，江西的平静和苏州的七十人被捕，都出自同一套结构，差别在于每个官员怎样接住同一份压力。
edits.after: 这也不是一个智者对抗暴君的故事。孔飞力列举过官僚抵制的几种情形：有深思熟虑的，有程序颟顸误了时机的，有因不信其事而轻视此案的，有怕清剿危及仕途的，也可能有耿直官员拒绝依据诬告迫害无辜。他说这些行动不像是协调一致的，抵制专制权力并不需要串通。孔飞力把江西也算作这样的例子：他推断，吴绍诗“根本就不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子”，这最接近因不信其事而轻视此案的一种。这是孔飞力从档案作出的推断。孔飞力也提醒，说弘历“利用”了政治罪，并不比说政治罪“利用”了他更接近真实。本文作者的一种解读是，江西的平静和苏州的七十人被捕，都出自同一套结构，差别在于每个官员怎样接住同一份压力。

edits.before: Nor is this a story of a wise man outwitting a tyrant. Kuhn lists several forms that bureaucratic resistance may have taken. Some was deliberate. Some came from sluggish procedures that kept officials from reacting to an emergency in time. Some officials, doubting the whole thing, may have refused to take the cases seriously. Others may have feared that the suppression campaign would endanger their careers. And some upright officials may have refused to persecute innocent people on the strength of false accusations. Kuhn writes that these actions do not look coordinated, and that resisting despotic power does not require collusion. This article cannot say which of these describes Wu Shaoshi. Kuhn also cautions that saying Hongli "used" political crime is no closer to the truth than saying political crime "used" him. My own reading is that the quiet in Jiangxi and the seventy arrests in Suzhou came out of the same structure. What differed was how each official handled the same pressure.
edits.after: Nor is this a story of a wise man outwitting a tyrant. Kuhn lists several forms that bureaucratic resistance may have taken. Some was deliberate. Some came from sluggish procedures that kept officials from reacting to an emergency in time. Some officials, doubting the whole thing, may have refused to take the cases seriously. Others may have feared that the suppression campaign would endanger their careers. And some upright officials may have refused to persecute innocent people on the strength of false accusations. Kuhn writes that these actions do not look coordinated, and that resisting despotic power does not require collusion. Kuhn counts Jiangxi among these cases: he infers that Wu Shaoshi never intended to pursue a case he regarded as a false rumour, which comes closest to the officials who doubted the whole thing. edits.before: Back to June. The rumours had crossed the border, and Wu Shaoshi sent no report. He later told Hongli that he had verbally ordered his subordinates to keep an eye on suspicious travellers, but no one had been arrested and no cases of queue-clipping had turned up in the province. On the failure to report the rumours, the emperor rebuked him only mildly: "You were wrong." Kuhn calls it an unexpected show of restraint toward an elderly and highly respected governor.
